title: Fix captive portal sign-in URL (#11961)
head: 7fec27a68e87
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Arch's packaged connectivity URI keeps the original sign-in URL on stock installs
leads.consequence: On a standard Omarchy install with unmodified NetworkManager settings, --print-config includes [connectivity] uri=http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt. resolveCaptivePortalUrl accepts that HTTP URL, so the user clicking Sign in still opens the same Arch URL the PR says portals ignore; the GNOME fallback only applies when a URI is absent, HTTPS, malformed or inaccessible. Either change the shipped connectivity config as well, or explicitly handle the stock Arch URI if the new fallback is intended for these users.

leads.summary: One-shot disk-config read drifts from NetworkManager's live URI
leads.consequence: The Process runs once when this widget is constructed. If NetworkManager reloads a changed connectivity URI while the shell stays open, the manager checks the new endpoint and emits a portal state, but the button opens the old URI until the shell restarts. Conversely, changing the disk file without reloading NM makes --print-config use the new endpoint before the manager does. A systemd service override of --connectivity-uri is likewise absent from the panel's bare print-config invocation. The daemon exposes its live ConnectivityCheckUri D-Bus property and notifies when it changes; read that rather than launch a second instance once.

leads.summary: Related open #13200 replaces the same action and tests with an incompatible sign-in view
leads.consequence: #13200 changes openCaptivePortal to launch omarchy-network-portal-signin with Model.captivePortalUrl, keep the panel open, and assert a view was used rather than a browser. This PR changes the same block to launch the browser with root.captivePortalUrl and closes the panel. A three-way merge of the two diverged heads has conflict markers both in Panel.qml and the fixture, and merely resolving the conflict by choosing one side defeats the other PR's behaviour. #13200 also has a test requiring a literal direct assignment to captivePortalUrl (changed here into an alias) and a grep for the sign-in helper called with Model.captivePortalUrl, so either naive combination fails its test. Coordinate the action, effective URI and test expectations; #13200 is not stacked on this PR.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F5; published as related open PR note

leads.summary: Valid case-insensitive HTTP connectivity URIs are silently replaced with the GNOME URL
leads.consequence: NetworkManager's URI checker explicitly accepts the scheme with g_ascii_strcasecmp (HTTP and Http as well as http). A user-specified `uri=HTTP://example.test/probe` can therefore be the endpoint NM probed, but this validator compares only exact `http://` and sends the browser to GNOME instead. On a portal that intercepts its configured hostname but not GNOME's, sign-in still fails. Accept the HTTP scheme case-insensitively while retaining the credential and other validation.

leads.summary: Open #6807 notification sign-in and this panel choose different URLs for the same portal
leads.consequence: If both non-stacked PRs merge, the panel opens the configured NM URI or GNOME fallback while #6807's `--url`/`--open` notification action always returns `http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt` regardless of the NM URI its own check_uri helper reads. A user at a portal where Arch's probe is not intercepted gets a working panel button but a broken notification sign-in button; changing this PR's fallback alone does not keep the new sibling action in sync. Share one resolved URI or align the notification launcher with the same policy.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (sol/pr-6807.diff:170-175 print_url returns fixed ping.archlinux.org); dropped: concerns #6807's own behaviour, not this PR

leads.summary: Fixture cannot detect ignoring NetworkManager's URI in the actual panel
leads.consequence: The new Node tests validate Model.resolveCaptivePortalUrl in isolation; the QML mock prints exactly the same GNOME URL that the panel initially has as fallback. If the onStreamFinished handler ignores `text` and always calls resolveCaptivePortalUrl with an empty string, the browser log still has the expected GNOME URL, and the structural regexp still sees `resolveCaptivePortalUrl`. This mutant passes every kept test in a compositor-free run; with a compositor, the mock and browser assertion likewise cannot distinguish it because the two URLs are identical. Change the mock to a distinct HTTP URI and assert the browser receives that URI, with a separate missing/failed-config fallback case.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3b (Sol mutant run plan-mutant); published as optional test improvement

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the code does what the description says. It reads `[connectivity] uri=` from `NetworkManager --print-config`, keeps it only when it is a credential-free `http://` URI, and otherwise falls back to `http://nmcheck.gnome.org/check_network_status.txt`. The URL is still passed as a single argv element. The new Node tests pass on this head and on a trial merge with the current `quattro` tip (`3faafba2`, no conflicts), and they fail against the pre-PR `Model.js`.

The main issue: on a default Omarchy install, once NetworkManager's configuration has been read, the button opens the same URL as before, so the problem in #11961 remains for users who have not changed that configuration.

| NetworkManager `[connectivity] uri` | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Arch default: `http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt` | `ping.archlinux.org` | `ping.archlinux.org` (unchanged) |
| Changed by hand to `http://nmcheck.gnome.org/…` (the #11961 reporter's setup) | `ping.archlinux.org` | `nmcheck.gnome.org`, read when the shell starts |
| An `https://` or otherwise unusable URI, or `--print-config` fails | `ping.archlinux.org` | `nmcheck.gnome.org` fallback |

### The default configuration still opens `ping.archlinux.org`

Arch's `networkmanager` package (1.58.1) installs `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/20-connectivity.conf` with `uri=http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt`, and Omarchy does not override it (its only NetworkManager drop-ins set Wi-Fi power saving and `[global-dns]`). `resolveCaptivePortalUrl` therefore returns the Arch URL, and the PR's own test asserts this ("follows NM even when it still uses Arch's probe"). The new comment in `Model.js` says this host "is often ignored", yet on stock installs the button still uses it.

`archlinux.org` is in the Chromium and Firefox HSTS preload lists with subdomains included, and `ping.archlinux.org` is reported as preloaded. Omarchy's default browser is Chromium. The likely effect:

```text
Default install (Arch config: uri=http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt)
 ├─ NetworkManager probe: curl, plain HTTP, no HSTS
 │    → portal intercepts port 80 → state PORTAL → "Open Captive Portal" button shown
 └─ Button: NetworkManager --print-config → same http://ping.archlinux.org/… URL
      → browser applies HSTS preload for archlinux.org and subdomains
      → request sent as https://ping.archlinux.org/… → portal cannot redirect it
```

The HSTS step comes from the published preload lists and NetworkManager's source, not from a browser run against a real portal.

**Impact:** on default installs the change does not alter the URL the button opens, so "Fixes #11961" holds only for users who have overridden NetworkManager's connectivity URI with a host that is not HSTS-covered. For the others, the button likely leads to a certificate, HSTS or timeout error (at best the browser's own captive-portal page) instead of the portal's login page. The GNOME fallback has a smaller form of the same risk: `gnome.org` is not preloaded, but `https://gnome.org/` sends `Strict-Transport-Security` with `includeSubDomains; preload`, so a browser that has visited it will also upgrade `nmcheck.gnome.org`.

**Suggested change:** make the button open a plain-HTTP URL on a host without HSTS on default installs. Optional approaches:
- ignore NetworkManager's URI when its host is HSTS-covered (at least `*.archlinux.org`) and use the fallback;
- ship an Omarchy NetworkManager connectivity override, so the probe and the button agree on one non-HSTS host (a product and privacy choice);
- always open a fixed URL on a host that does not use HTTPS, for example `http://neverssl.com/`, which is in neither preload list.

Until one of these is in place, the description could say "Refs #11961" rather than "Fixes", so merging does not close the issue.

### The URL is read once at shell start, from disk

The `Process` running `NetworkManager --print-config` runs once when the panel is created and is never re-run. NetworkManager's man page says `--print-config` "reads configuration files from disk", which can differ from what the running daemon has loaded.

**Impact:** if a user changes the connectivity URI (as the #11961 reporter did) and reloads NetworkManager, the daemon probes the new URI, but the button keeps the old one until the shell restarts. This contradicts the PR's comment, "so sign-in matches the probe NM used".

**Suggested change:** read the running daemon's `ConnectivityCheckUri` D-Bus property (`org.freedesktop.NetworkManager`, readable without privileges), for example with `busctl get-property` when `hasCaptivePortal` becomes true or on click. This removes both the staleness and the gap between disk and daemon. Quickshell's networking module does not expose this property, so a `Process` is still needed.

### Parser differs from NetworkManager's key-file rules

`parseNetworkManagerConnectivityUri` lowercases both the group and the key, but NetworkManager reads only the exact `[connectivity]` group and `uri` key. With `uri=http://ping.archlinux.org/…` followed by `URI=http://example.test/check`, NetworkManager uses the first and the parser returns the second. The parser also requires a lower-case `http://`, while NetworkManager accepts the scheme in any case, so `HTTP://…` falls back to the GNOME URL.

**Impact:** in these cases the button opens a different URL from the one NetworkManager probes. Both need an unusual configuration.

**Suggested change:** match `[connectivity]` and `uri` exactly, and compare the scheme case-insensitively, to mirror NetworkManager.

**Optional test improvement:** two of the new checks do not catch the regressions they appear to guard against.
- `assert(!/ping\\.archlinux\\.org/.test(panelSource), …)` sits inside a quoted heredoc (`<<'JS'`), so the regex looks for literal backslashes and never matches `ping.archlinux.org`. With `Panel.qml` changed to launch `http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt` directly, the assertion still reports ok (the Node half passes; only the runtime browser-log check, which needs a compositor and was skipped here, would notice that edit). With the regex written as `/ping\.archlinux\.org/`, the assertion fails as intended.
- The runtime fixture's `NetworkManager` stub prints the fallback URL, and the browser-log check compares against that same URL, so the check passes even if the panel ignores the `--print-config` result. A stub URI that differs from the fallback, such as `http://portal-probe.test/check`, with the fixture waiting until the panel has picked it up before activating the button, would test the wiring.

**Related open PR:** #13200 ("Sign in to captive portals in a dropdown instead of the browser") rewrites the same `openCaptivePortal()` lines and runtime-test hunk. Its diff applies to the current tip but not on top of this PR. It launches its sign-in view with `Model.captivePortalUrl`, which after this PR is the GNOME fallback rather than the resolved `root.captivePortalUrl`. Whichever PR lands second needs to choose the URL source explicitly.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head, the merge-base and the current `quattro` tip, plus NetworkManager 1.58.1, Arch's `networkmanager` packaging, Quickshell's `Process` and networking sources, and the Chromium and Firefox HSTS preload lists. Sandboxed runs covered the PR's test on the head, on a trial merge with the tip and against the pre-PR code; a parser probe with synthetic NetworkManager configurations; and a mutated `Panel.qml` for the vacuous assertion. The QML runtime half of the test was skipped (no compositor). No real NetworkManager daemon, browser or captive portal was used, so the HSTS effect is inferred from the preload lists rather than observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
